facts.evidence: gh api repos/aspose-gis-foss/Aspose.GIS.FOSS-for-.Net/readme returns HTTP 404. Repository root contents: .gitignore, Aspose.GIS.FOSS.Tests/, Aspose.GIS.FOSS.slnx, Aspose.GIS.FOSS/ -- no README file of any name.

facts.claim: N/A -- independent reproduction of the old repository's 2026-10-19 finding (docs/DECISION_LOG.md: 'incomplete upload: imported namespaces defined nowhere; dotnet build 369 errors'), not assumed true from that citation
facts.evidence: Fresh `git clone --depth 1` of this exact repository followed by `dotnet build Aspose.GIS.FOSS.slnx -c Release` (full log: dotnet_build_log.txt, this directory) produces 381 compile errors (close to, not identical to, the old repo's cited 369 -- plausibly a different .NET SDK version or a few commits of drift; the core finding is the same). Representative error classes: CS0246 'type or namespace name could not be found' for Axis, GeometryType, Extent, BoundingBox, SpatialReferenceSystem, Unit, Projection, Identifier, GeographicDatum, Ellipsoid, PointsSequence, LayerIndices, LayerEvaluationRestrictions, MapInfoCoordinateValidationException/Error, WrapAttributesConverter -- all referenced throughout the main project (Geometries/, SpatialReferencing/, VectorLayer.cs, FeaturesSequence.cs) but defined nowhere in the uploaded source tree; plus CS0535/CS0534/CS0115/CS0508 interface/override mismatches consistent with the same missing-type root cause. The bundled test project (Aspose.GIS.FOSS.Tests/MainTests.cs) also fails to compile, referencing VectorLayer, Drivers, Dataset, GeoPackageDataset -- none resolvable. A stray Class1.cs (a `dotnet new classlib` default stub) is still present at the project root, consistent with an incomplete/placeholder upload rather than a finished product with a missing README.

disposition_for_both_lanes: NON_PROCESSABLE. Neither Lane L nor Lane R may proceed: there is no README to correct (Lane L has nothing to anchor to), and composing a full from-scratch Lane R README for a product whose own source does not compile would require inventing capability claims, installation instructions, and working examples for code that does not exist in a working form -- explicitly forbidden by mission section 7 ('Handle weak/nonprocessable repositories honestly; no fabricated application, code examples, package versions, or publication claims'). This independently reproduces and confirms the old repository's own 2026-10-19 classification of this exact repository as blocked upstream, rather than inheriting it unverified.
